Inter-company validation — Financials

Balance sheet & P&L intercompany balances. Each entity's intercompany balances are summarised by a unique IC Code (e.g. IC-001-US-OIL). Split each IC Code across its counterparties — in any order — capturing the counterparty, their currency and their own local-currency amount. A SUMIF check confirms each IC Code's splits tie to the summary, and counterparty amounts are compared in USD.

Intercompany split

Inter-company validation — Cash flows

Intercompany cash-flow movements (operating & financing). Each entity's intercompany cash flows are summarised by a unique IC Code (e.g. ICF-001-US-OIL). Split each IC Code across its counterparties — in any order — capturing the counterparty, their currency, their own local-currency amount and the corresponding cash-flow account. A SUMIF check confirms each IC Code's splits tie to the summary, and counterparty amounts are compared in USD at the average rate.

Group balance sheet

Every entity translated into the group presentation currency and consolidated. The GROUP column sums all entities; each entity column shows its figures translated from its local currency. A translation reserve (CTA) balances each translated balance sheet.

No reporting period selected

Choose or create a reporting period first.

Not validated flags entities whose financials haven't passed validation yet

Group profit & loss

Every entity translated into the group presentation currency at average rate and consolidated. The GROUP column is the sum of all entities; each entity column shows its income statement translated from its local currency.

No reporting period selected

Choose or create a reporting period first.

Not validated flags entities whose financials haven't passed validation yet

Group journal entries

Consolidation adjustments posted at group level in USD. Each posted entry adds a JE column to the relevant statement; the Adjustment column sums all entries, and Final = Group + Adjustment. Entries hitting the P&L automatically update Current year profit/(loss) on the balance sheet.

Import entities

Upload a CSV file. Required columns: legal_name, country, currency. Write the full country name (e.g. "France") — the entity code is generated automatically. Optional: address, tax_id, company_id, gaap, language, reporting_period, incorporation, activity.
For contacts: contact1_name, contact1_title, contact1_email, contact1_phone, contact2_name… (unlimited).

One row per entity

Only legal_name, country and currency are required. Write the country's full name, not its code. The entity code (e.g. FR01) is generated for you. Add as many contacts as you like with numbered columns.

legal_namecountrycurrencygaapincorporationcontact1_namecontact1_email
Acme France SASFranceEURFrench GAAP14/03/2012Marie Duboism.dubois@acme.fr
Acme Madagascar SARLMadagascarMGAPCG 200502/06/2018Rivo Heryr.hery@acme.mg

Rows with a missing required field or an unrecognised country are rejected and listed back with the reason; the good rows still import.

Bulk import accounts

Upload the Excel workbook — one tab per statement: statement lines with their code, accounts with theirs beneath them, and an Intercompany Yes/No on every tab. Download the template below to get the current chart in that shape; edit it, add rows (leave Code empty — numbering is automatic), and upload it back. Re-uploads recognise codes, so renames update rather than duplicate. The legacy 12-column CSV is still accepted.

One row per component

statement is BS, PL, OCI or CF. code is just the number — the prefix comes from the statement and the category (BS-NCA-001, PL-EXP-001, OCI→PL-OCI-001, CF-INV-001). category must already exist and match the statement. Debit/credit comes from the category, so there is no balance column.

fs_caption names the line this component prints on. If that caption doesn't exist in the category yet, it is created. Leave it blank and the component lands in Unassigned.

statementcategorycodenamefs_captionintercompanycounterpartyequity_reservecf_adjustmentbs_accountcf_captionbs_caption
BSNCA001Land and buildingsProperty, plant and equipmentNoNo
BSCA001Intercompany receivablesTrade and other receivablesYesMU02;MU03No
BSEQ003Translation reserveOther reservesNoNo
PLEXP001DepreciationOperating expensesNoYesBS-NCA-001Adjustments for
OCIOCI001Foreign exchange translationItems that may be reclassifiedNoBS-EQ-003No
CFINV001Purchase of PPEInvesting activitiesNoNoProperty, plant and equipment

The three rules the form enforces are enforced here too. An OCI row must name an existing equity_reserve. A CF row must name an existing bs_caption — every cash movement explains a balance sheet movement. A P&L row with cf_adjustment=Yes must name a bs_account; it then mirrors into the cash flow chart under the same code, as a single figure. Use cf_caption to say which operating caption it lands on.

counterparty is read only when intercompany is Yes. Rows may reference a caption or an account that another row in the same file creates, so one file can build the whole chart. Anything missing a field, with an unknown category, or a duplicate code is listed back to you with the reason.

Bulk import FX rates

Upload a CSV with columns: currency_code, opening_rate, average_rate, closing_rate. Only currencies already used by a subsidiary are accepted; leave a rate blank to keep the existing value.

One row per foreign currency

Rates are how many of the group's presentation currency equal 1 unit of the foreign currency. Use the opening, period-average and closing rates. Leave a cell blank to keep what's already there.

currency_codeopening_rateaverage_rateclosing_rate
EUR485049004950
USD445045004520

(Example for a group presenting in MGA: 1 EUR = 4,900 MGA average.)

Import shareholders (first-time)

For entities that have no shareholders yet. Download the template — every such entity is listed for you — fill in the Type, Shareholder and % Holding for each, then upload. This is for the first assignment only; later changes use “Change shareholding”.

One row per shareholder — repeat the entity code on each row

pct is the ownership %. Every row for the same entity must add up to 100. Fill effective_date once (first row of the entity). For Related entity put the shareholder's entity code; for Individual / Non-related put a name.

Example — entity FR01 with 10 shareholders (mix of types), totalling 100%:

entity_codeentity_nameeffective_datetypeshareholderpct
FR01Acme France SAS01/01/2026Related entityMG0130
FR01Acme France SASRelated entityDE0115
FR01Acme France SASIndividualJohn Smith10
FR01Acme France SASIndividualMarie Dubois8
FR01Acme France SASIndividualRivo Hery7
FR01Acme France SASIndividualPaul Martin5
FR01Acme France SASNon-relatedBpifrance10
FR01Acme France SASNon-relatedCrédit Agricole6
FR01Acme France SASNon-relatedABC Holdings Ltd5
FR01Acme France SASNon-relatedXYZ Capital4

Then start a new block of rows for the next entity (MG01, …). Allowed type values: Related entity, Individual, Non-related.

New financial statement caption

A caption is the line that prints on the face of the statement. Components roll into it.

NCA-

Every OCI caption is a column in the statement of changes in equity — components under it inherit this reserve.

Each cash flow line explains the movement of a balance sheet component — accounts under it inherit this link, and can override it when they point at a different component.

System caption — only the code number can be changed.

Pick the profit or loss component

This item lives in the P&L. Link an existing component so there is only ever one figure.
